_about: Public-domain Nehemiah Adams (1806-1878), Congregational minister of the Essex Street Church, Boston, for the Word Hoard: Remarks on the Unitarian Belief (1832), The Baptized Child (1842), The Life of John Eliot (1847), The Friends of Christ in the New Testament (1853), Christ a Friend (1854), A South-Side View of Slavery (1854), The Communion Sabbath (1856), Agnes and the Key of her Little Coffin (1857), The Reasonableness of Future, Endless Punishment (1858), Why am I a Trinitarian Congregationalist? (1858) and Catharine (1859). from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 60 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

nadams-unitarian-belief: Remarks on the Unitarian belief : with a letter to a Unitarian friend on the Lord's supper (Boston : Peirce and Parker, 1832)
nadams-john-eliot: The life of John Eliot; with an account of the early missionary efforts among the Indians of New England (Boston, Massachusetts Sabbath School Society, 1847)
nadams-friends-of-christ: The friends of Christ in the New Testament: thirteen discourses (Boston : T.R. Marvin, 1853)
nadams-christ-a-friend: Christ a friend : thirteen discourses (Boston : John P. Jewett, 1855)
nadams-south-side-view: A South-side view of slavery; or, Three months at the South in 1854 (Boston, T.R. Marvin, 1855)
nadams-agnes: Agnes and the key of her little coffin (Boston, S. K. Whipple and Company, 1857)
nadams-endless-punishment: The reasonableness of future, endless punishment / by Nehemiah Adams (Gould and Lincoln, 1858)
nadams-trinitarian: Why am I a Trinitarian Congregationalist? (catalogued 1858)
nadams-catharine: Catharine (Boston: J. E. Tilton and Company. New York: Sheldon & Co. London; Knight & Son, 1859)

_alternates.nadams-unitarian-belief: remarksonunitari00adam (the same 1832 printing; its title page is garbled in the OCR) swapped for this Google scan, whose title page reads 'By Nehemiah Adams, Pastor of the First Church of Christ in Cambridge'

_excluded.nadams-other: Thomas Shepard's Autobiography (1832), which he only edited; the 1859 Discussion of future punishment (a debate with others); the Essex Street memorial volume (by the church)

_identity_checked.nadams-baptized-child: title page (after the Google notice): 'The Baptized Child, BrNEHEMIAH ADAMS [by Nehemiah Adams]', Massachusetts Sabbath School Society; copyright 'in the year 1836, by Nehemiah Adams'
_identity_checked.nadams-john-eliot: title page: 'The Life of John Eliot, with an account of the early missionary efforts among the Indians of New England, by Nehemlah [Nehemiah] Adams, Pastor of Essex Street Church, Boston'
_identity_checked.nadams-agnes: published anonymously, 'by her father' (Boston: S. K. Whipple, 1857); the Library of Congress copy is catalogued under Nehemiah Adams, and Catharine (also on this shelf) is 'by the author of Agnes and the Little Key'
_identity_checked.nadams-catharine: published anonymously: title page 'Catharine, by the author of "Agnes and the Little Key"' (Boston: J. E. Tilton, 1859), dedicated 'to the young ladies of my congregation'; catalogued under Nehemiah Adams

nadams-agnes.ia_possible_copyright_status: The Library of Congress is unaware of any copyright restrictions for this item.
